q: A major criterion of rheumatic fever is:
e: Fever, PR and ESR are minor.

q: Each of the following is a major criterion of rheumatic fever EXCEPT:
Regarding carditis of acute rheumatic fever, which is TRUE?
o: Aortic regurgitation is the commonest lesion
It is characterised by valve involvement
Early treatment does not change valve involvement
Valve damage never follows asymptomatic carditis
e: Mitral regurgitation is commonest; echo finds subclinical carditis.

q: All are true of rheumatic fever EXCEPT:
o: A systolic murmur may be heard
It usually follows pneumonia 2–6 weeks earlier
Migratory arthritis is a major criterion

q: A patient with rheumatic heart disease has fever for 2 weeks. The most likely diagnosis is:
e: Fever in RHD = IE until proved otherwise.

q: A 10-year-old girl has a painful swollen right knee, fever, an apical diastolic murmur, high ESR and positive ASO. The diagnosis is:
e: 2 major (arthritis, carditis) + GAS evidence (Carey Coombs murmur).

q: The drug of choice for secondary prophylaxis of rheumatic fever is:
o: Benzathine penicillin G IM every 4 weeks

q: A 22 kg child with ARF needs benzathine penicillin. The dose is:
An apical diastolic rumble, loud S1 and opening snap indicate:
e: Rheumatic MS takes years to develop.
